evidence_quotes.agenda: 'Do you want to share any other specific concerns or what are you most worried about for the upcoming move, I'd like to address each one of them' — asked well, but only after the full inventory/address probe was already done.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: First pass got 'cost is number one on everybody's list'; rep pushed again ('anything that you're stressed about for the upcoming move?') and the real concern surfaced — 'that's the stress... we're older and it's been eight years... we're both senior citizens' — which she then engaged with warmly rather than brushing past.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: 'you are not [bound] by this estimate... you mentioned earlier that you are planning to move some boxes, that's a good game plan... preparation [pays off]' (window + self-prep) and 'does that sound good so far?' answered with an immediate 'Yes, yeah' (no re-pitch) read as the fairness check.

top_strength: Best call in the batch — textbook quid pro quo open, genuinely dug past the surface concern to the real one (age/stress about the move), and tied the self-prep tip back to something the customer had already volunteered.
coaching_note: This is the rubric's own model of the agenda + two-layers-deep flow (just landing after logistics instead of before) — the one gap left is that neither differentiator sheet (damage coverage, Meet Your Mover) ever gets named, even with two senior, anxious customers who'd likely respond well to the reassurance.
